back2basics.concept: Judicial Review and Legal Rights against Detention
back2basics.text: Judicial review is the power of courts to examine the actions of the executive and legislature to ensure they comply with the law and constitution. Legal safeguards protect individuals from arbitrary arrest and detention, requiring due process and adherence to procedural rules. Courts can intervene if detentions are unlawful or politically motivated, ensuring the rule of law is maintained.

2026-11-02-pm-09f668cf34.deck: Senior Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan moved the Supreme Court seeking relief after the Enforcement Directorate detained him immediately upon his release on bail outside Rampur Jail. The case raises important questions on legal rights against detention and the judiciary's role in checking executive actions.

2026-11-02-pm-90626c839b.anchor: E-governance and Digital Transformation in Aviation

back2basics.text: Digital boarding systems use technology such as facial recognition and mobile applications to enable contactless passenger processing at airports. E-passports contain embedded electronic chips storing biometric and personal data, facilitating secure and faster identity verification during travel. Digi Yatra leverages these technologies to streamline airport procedures while complementing existing travel document checks.

2026-11-02-pm-90626c839b.deck: The Ministry of Civil Aviation started Digi Yatra trials for international passengers at seven Indian airports from November to December 2026. This initiative tests digital boarding using e-passports and facial recognition, aiming for a wider rollout in 2027.

body.text: Eligible passengers create an e-passport-based Verifiable Credential by scanning the Machine Readable Zone and embedded chip using NFC, capturing a selfie, and verifying details via the Digi Yatra app.

body.label: Credential storage
body.text: The Verifiable Credential is stored in the passenger's Digi Yatra wallet on their smartphone and used at enabled airport touchpoints.

body.label: Complementary process
body.text: Digi Yatra complements existing travel procedures; passengers must still carry travel documents and complete airline and immigration checks.

body.label: User base and expansion
body.text: The platform already has over 26.5 million users and has facilitated more than 110 million journeys across 39 domestic airports, with plans to cover 25 more by 2027.

body.label: Government vision
body.text: The initiative aligns with the Government of India's Digital India and Ease of Flying visions to make air travel seamless and technology-driven.

back2basics.text: Coal is a major source of energy in India, used primarily for power generation and industrial fuel. Coal production involves extracting coal from mines, while overburden removal is the process of clearing soil and rock above coal seams to access the coal. Offtake refers to the quantity of coal supplied to consumers. Efficient coal production and supply are critical for maintaining energy security, reducing imports, and supporting industrial growth.

2026-11-02-pm-b889f5e7f6.deck: Western Coalfields Limited (WCL), a subsidiary of Coal India Limited (CIL), exceeded its production, offtake, and overburden removal targets from April to October 2026, driving CIL’s overall growth. This performance strengthens India’s domestic coal availability and energy security, a key topic for UPSC economy and environment syllabus.

body.label: Exceeded targets
body.text: WCL achieved 102.47% of its coal production target, 108.82% of its offtake target, and 104.56% of its overburden removal target from April to October 2026.

body.label: Strong monthly growth
body.text: In October 2026, WCL’s coal production grew 64.87% year-on-year to 5.93 MT, and offtake grew 50.16% to 6.67 MT, both highest among major CIL subsidiaries.

body.label: Overall growth rates
body.text: During April–October 2026, WCL’s coal production grew 15.92% to 32.96 MT, offtake grew 25.54% to 41.56 MT, and overburden removal grew 36.10% to 207.95 MCuM.

sections.heading: What operational achievements did WCL record in 2026?

body.label: Stock reduction
body.text: WCL reduced pithead coal stock from 13.034 MT on April 1, 2026 to 4.44 MT on October 31, 2026, liquidating around 8.6 MT or 66% of opening stock.

body.label: Rake loading increase
body.text: Rake loading increased by 39.6% to 6,146 rakes up to October 31, 2026, with power sector rakes up 40.8%, supporting better coal evacuation.

body.label: Coordination efforts
body.text: Enhanced coordination with Railways and focused monitoring of rake placement and loading were key to improved coal evacuation.

sections.heading: How did WCL improve coal stock and evacuation?

body.label: Mine-level monitoring
body.text: Daily reviews, regular meetings with Area General Managers, and senior management visits enabled faster resolution of operational bottlenecks.

body.label: Clearances and coordination
body.text: WCL secured four environmental clearances/amendments and two forest clearances in FY 2026–27, ensuring uninterrupted mining operations.

body.label: Technology upgrades
body.text: WCL operates six Surface Miners and three Continuous Miners, improved transportation infrastructure, rapid loading systems, and automated weighbridges.

back2basics.concept: Collegium System and Separation of Powers
back2basics.text: The collegium system is a method by which judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts are appointed and transferred, primarily involving senior judges rather than the executive. Separation of powers is a constitutional principle that divides government responsibilities among the legislature, executive, and judiciary to prevent concentration of power and ensure checks and balances. Judicial independence is essential to uphold this separation and maintain the rule of law.

back2basics.concept: Public Accounts Committees and Democratic Dissent
back2basics.text: Public Accounts Committees (PACs) are parliamentary committees responsible for examining government expenditure to ensure it complies with legislative approval and promotes accountability. Democratic dissent refers to the right and practice of expressing disagreement within a democracy, which helps bring new ideas, correct errors, and improve governance. Both PACs and dissent are essential for a functioning parliamentary democracy, ensuring transparency, accountability, and inclusive decision-making.
